title: Optimal Regularization for a Data Source
reviewed_version: arXiv:2212.13597v4, revised 2024-09-10; equivalence to the journal-final version is not asserted
inspection_outcome: Three supported central derivation failures; five bounded local corrections; main population optimum verified under explicit assumptions
summary: Theorem 11 uses invalid pointwise brackets but has a verified repair. Theorem 14 uses an insufficient empirical L1 radius in a deterministic complexity bound. Section 6.2 uses a false convex-body metric entropy order. The full probability/risk theorems are not claimed refuted by those intermediate examples. Main Theorems 3/4 and common-kernel compactness hold under their stated feasible hypotheses.

issues.claim: Theorem11 original constant brackets fail pointwise.
issues.evidence: Exp(1), r=1/4, shifted unit intervals, x=4: 400/49-204/25=4/1225>0; failure has positive probability.
issues.correction: Use C eta ||x|| instead of C M_P eta; integrable finite bracketing proves ULLN.
issues.counterevidence: Theorem conclusion survives the checked repair; no theorem refutation asserted.

independent_acceptance.focused_reasoning: Theorem 11 uses constant-width brackets despite a Lipschitz bound growing with |x|. For r=1/4 and intervals [-.5,.5],[-.51,.49], the gauge difference violates the written 16*eta constant at x>98/25, on positive-probability exponential tails. Brackets with an integrable |x| envelope and finite nets repair the ULLN, but the stated central pointwise bracketing step is false.

issues.claim: Theorem14 deterministic finite-class estimate uses inadequate empirical L1 radius.
issues.evidence: 16 ellipsoid gauges on basis sample: exact Rademacher complexity>0.0624 while asserted limiting upper bound<0.0374.
issues.correction: Empirical L2 radius or uniform envelope in finite-net bound.
issues.counterevidence: No direct refutation of final high-probability theorem including concentration term.

independent_acceptance.focused_reasoning: The m=d=16 ellipsoidal gauges on samples e_i meet the actual ambient inradius class. With tau=.001, the exact Rademacher maximum is (1-tau)(1-2^-15)/16, exceeding the asserted empirical-L1 radius bound. An empirical L2 radius or envelope is required. The deterministic central step is refuted; the full probability/risk conclusion is not claimed disproved by this sample.

issues.claim: Corollary5 proof uses false logarithmic convex-body entropy.
issues.evidence: 2^n convex bodies conv((1/2)B union selected n circle points), Hausdorff separated by 1-cos(2pi/n); log covering at h/3 >= n log2, not O(log n).
issues.correction: Recompute entropy-dependent rate; correct radial union identity and cover-centre selection.
issues.counterevidence: Packing refutes ambient bound; not claimed unit-volume packing or direct final risk counterexample.

independent_acceptance.focused_reasoning: The 2^n convex bodies obtained from a half-radius disk and subsets of n unit-circle points have Hausdorff separation at least 1-cos(2*pi/n); logarithmic covering entropy grows proportionally to n rather than log n. The page image confirms the source really prints the logarithmic ambient-class bound. The union radial function is a maximum; reciprocal and restricted-centre cover steps need local repairs. No counterexample to the final unit-volume constrained risk theorem is inferred solely from the ambient packing.

issues.evidence: P1=delta0, P2=(delta0+delta1)/2, Phi=-log4 gives TV^2=1/4 > log2/8.
issues.correction: Bound exp(-Phi)<=M and use factor2 M^2/Z1^2.
issues.counterevidence: Nonnegative Gaussian potential example not refuted.

independent_acceptance.focused_reasoning: For constant potential -log(4), likelihood 4, priors delta_0 and (delta_0+delta_1)/2, posterior TV squared is 1/4 while the stated KL-based right side is log(2)/8. A likelihood upper bound supplies the missing factor; the nonnegative-potential Gaussian example is preserved.

issues.claim: Explicit Gaussian optimum has wrong volume normalization.
issues.evidence: Printed scale produces volume kappa_d^2; d2 SigmaI gives area pi^2.
issues.counterevidence: General main formula and Gaussian shape remain valid.

independent_acceptance.focused_reasoning: The displayed positive power kappa_d^(1/d) produces volume kappa_d^2 for the proposed ellipsoid. The inverse power is the determined volume-one correction.

issues.evidence: Containing rB and volume1 requires kappa_d r^d<=1.
issues.counterevidence: Compactness and feasible minimizer convergence remain valid.

independent_acceptance.focused_reasoning: The unit-volume class containing a radius-r ball is empty when r>kappa_d^(-1/d). Compactness/minimizer assertions require a nonempty feasible radius; the report retains the valid feasible-domain result.

issues.claim: Continuous density with finite second moment need not give positive radial moment.
issues.evidence: Smooth probability density supported in B(3e1,1) has zero radial moments for u1<=0.
issues.correction: Retain explicit positive continuous radial-moment hypothesis.

independent_acceptance.focused_reasoning: A smooth density supported in a ball away from the origin is continuous with finite second moment but has zero radial moment in a hemisphere. This refutes the claimed sufficient condition, not the theorem that explicitly assumes a positive radial moment.

issues.claim: Absolute continuity alone cannot identify KL and cross-entropy minimizers when all KL values are infinite.
issues.evidence: Disjoint smooth symmetric bumps with a_n=2^(-n-1), w_n=a_n exp(-4^n), finite second moment and infinite integral p logp; interval gauge objective1/a+1/b uniquely minimized while all KL infinite.

independent_acceptance.focused_reasoning: Smooth disjoint symmetric bumps with mass a_n=2^(-n-1) and width a_n*exp(-4^n) give finite second moment but infinite integral p log p. Absolute continuity alone therefore does not make the KL objective finite, although the corresponding gauge objective remains finite and minimized symmetrically. The report's restriction of the equivalence is justified.

checked_results.claim: Theorems3 and4: explicit optimal star body, existence and uniqueness
checked_results.method: Independent Holder proof and assumption audit
reasoning: For alpha>0, define rho_L(u)^(d+alpha)=integral_0^infinity r^(d+alpha-1)p(ru)dr. Positivity and continuity on the compact sphere bound rho_L above and away from0, producing a compact star body containing0 in its interior.

Polar coordinates and nonnegative Tonelli give F_alpha(K)=integral_sphere rho_K^(-alpha)rho_L^(d+alpha)du. Since the radial moment is continuous finite, E||X||_2^alpha=integral_sphere rho_L^(d+alpha)du<infinity; the apparent use of only a first-moment hypothesis for alpha>1 is not a gap because the radial hypothesis already supplies the required moment.
Write integral rho_L^d = integral [rho_K^(-alpha)rho_L^(d+alpha)]^(d/(d+alpha)) [rho_K^d]^(alpha/(d+alpha)). Holder gives F_alpha(K)>=d vol(L)^((d+alpha)/d)vol(K)^(-alpha/d).

Equality requires rho_K proportional to rho_L almost everywhere. Continuity makes this equality hold everywhere; fixed unit volume selects the unique K*=vol(L)^(-1/d)L. This proves the alpha=1 case as well.
No symmetry assumption is needed. Ifp is even, rho_L is even and the optimum is centrally symmetric, but nonsymmetric star bodies are allowed.

reasoning: A star-body gauge is convex exactly when its unit sublevel body is convex. Multiplying the gauge by a positive normalization constant does not change convexity.

For densities p(x)=psi(||x||_L), substituting t=r||u||_L yields rho_P(u)=c rho_L(u), hence the unit-volume optimal body is vol(L)^(-1/d)L. This covers uniform-star-body and nonsingular centered-Gaussian densities.

For0<alpha<1, no nonzero positive alpha-homogeneous function can be convex: f(tx)=t^alpha f(x)>t f(x)+(1-t)f(0) for0<t<1. Corollary5 is a conditional statement whose convexity premise is impossible in that range, not a false positive conclusion.

checked_results.method: Independent analytic verification on the stated common-kernel class
reasoning: If rB is contained inkerK, thenK is the union overu inK ofconv(rB,u). Every such convex body has a globally1/r-Lipschitz gauge; taking the infimum preserves the1/r Lipschitz bound. Thus the gauge ofK itself is1/r-Lipschitz.

For unitu, rho_K(u),rho_L(u)>=r, so |1/rho_K-1/rho_L|<=delta(K,L)/r^2. Combined with the gauge Lipschitz bound this proves the first inequality ofProposition2; integrating the homogeneous bound yieldsCorollary2.
For convex bodies with rB subsetK,L subsetRB andgamma=d_H(K,L), K subset L+gammaB subset(1+gamma/r)L and vice versa. This givesdelta<=Rgamma/r and therefore the claimed gauge boundRgamma/r^3.

For a bounded sequence inS(r), gauges on the sphere are bounded between1/R and1/r and are uniformly1/r-Lipschitz. Arzela-Ascoli supplies a uniformly convergent subsequence to a positive continuous gaugeg. Reciprocals converge uniformly, hence both radial and Hausdorff convergence to the associated star bodyK.

The kernel condition survives: forz inrB andx inK choosex_n inK_n converging tox. Each segment[z,x_n] lies inK_n; Hausdorff convergence puts[z,x] inK. ThusrB subsetkerK. A closed constraint class retains the limit.
Volume is continuous under this convergence by volK=(1/d)integral rho_K^d and uniform boundedness. The volume-one subclass is closed.

A farthest pointx and the coneconv(rB intersectx^perp,x) give actual conevolume ||x|| kappa_(d-1)r^(d-1)/d<=1. This yields an outer bound at least as strong as the paper's looserR_r usingd+1. definitions_and_hypotheses.gauge: g_K(x)=||x||_K; g_K(0)=0; for x!=0, g_K(x)=||x||_2/rho_K(x/||x||_2). Star bodies have positive continuous radial function.
definitions_and_hypotheses.kernel_class: S^d(r)={K:r B^d subset ker(K)}, and S^d(r,1) also imposes volume(K)=1. In particular rho_K>=r and g_K(x)<=||x||_2/r.
definitions_and_hypotheses.feasibility: The minimizer assertions in S^d(r,1) require a nonempty class, equivalently 0<r<=kappa_d^{-1/d}; the supporting core helper checks this boundary. The later consistency arguments below are evaluated on this feasible class.
definitions_and_hypotheses.empirical_measure: P_m is the empirical measure of m independent identically distributed observations from P.
definitions_and_hypotheses.section5_moments: Theorems 8,9,11 assume E_P||X||_2<infinity. Theorem 13 assumes finite first moments for both P and noise Q.
definitions_and_hypotheses.section6_bounded_data: Theorem 14 and Corollaries 5-8 assume ||X||_2<=1 almost surely, a common contained r_C-ball, finite metric covers, and Lipschitz dependence of the gauge on the set in the sphere supremum norm. Theorem 14 does not require volume normalization.
definitions_and_hypotheses.posterior: Proposition 7 assumes P1 is absolutely continuous with respect to P2, a real-valued potential Phi and finite positive normalizers; it does not state Phi>=0 or an upper bound of one on exp(-Phi).

findings.title: Theorem 11 uses an expectation bound as a pointwise bracketing bound
findings.location: Theorem 11 proof, p20; dependency in Theorem 8 proof, pp20-21
findings.claim: The proof claims that brackets g_L+/-C M_P eta, with the lower truncated at zero, pointwise bound every gauge g_K within delta(K,L)<=eta, where C=1/r^2 and M_P=E||X||_2.
findings.failure: Corollary 2 bounds expectations. The pointwise bound has ||x||_2 in place of M_P, which is not a pointwise upper bound on the sample norm.

counterexample.assumptions: d=1, r=1/4, P=Exp(1) on [0,infinity), M_P=1, C=16; eta=1/100; epsilon=8/25; eta=epsilon/(2 C M_P).
counterexample.bodies: L=[-1/2,1/2] and K=[-51/100,49/100]. They are convex star bodies of length one, their kernels are themselves, and both contain [-1/4,1/4]. delta(K,L)=1/100.
counterexample.exact_check: For x>=0, g_L(x)=2x and g_K(x)=100x/49. The proposed upper bracket is 2x+4/25. Their difference is (2/49)x-4/25, positive precisely when x>98/25. At x=4 it equals 4/1225>0.
counterexample.non_null_failure: The failure region has P probability exp(-98/25)>0. It is not a discrepancy confined to a null set.
counterexample.net_scope: A finite eta-net may be enlarged to include L; hence the displayed implication for a centre satisfying delta<=eta is invalid under the proof's own stated construction.

corrected_proof: For unit u, rho_K(u),rho_L(u)>=r, so |g_K(u)-g_L(u)|=|rho_K(u)-rho_L(u)|/(rho_K(u)rho_L(u))<=delta(K,L)/r^2. Positive homogeneity extends this to all x: |g_K(x)-g_L(x)|<=C delta(K,L)||x||_2; at x=0 both sides vanish.

On a finite eta-net of the nonempty compact metric class S^d(r,1), define l_L(x)=max{g_L(x)-C eta||x||_2,0} and u_L(x)=g_L(x)+C eta||x||_2. Each is Borel measurable because the gauge and Euclidean norm are continuous.
If delta(K,L)<=eta, the pointwise estimate gives l_L<=g_K<=u_L. The gauges are nonnegative, which justifies truncating the lower bracket.
Since r B subset L, g_L(x)<=||x||_2/r. Thus 0<=l_L<=g_L and 0<=u_L<=(1/r+C eta)||x||_2. Both bracket endpoints are P-integrable under M_P<infinity.

Pointwise u_L-l_L<=2 C eta||x||_2, and consequently E_P(u_L-l_L)<=2 C eta M_P. For M_P>0 choose eta<epsilon/(2 C M_P) to meet the strict epsilon version of Theorem 10. The finite union of all lower and upper endpoints provides the required finite collection.
If M_P=0, X=0 almost surely; all gauges vanish on all observations and under P, so uniform convergence is immediate. No division by M_P is needed.

Measurability can also be made explicit without appealing to a potentially nonmeasurable supremum: compactness gives a countable delta-dense set. K maps to g_K(x), P_mg_K and Pg_K are continuous, the last two with Lipschitz constants C P_m||X|| and C M_P. Hence the supremum of |P_mg_K-Pg_K| equals the supremum over a countable dense set and is measurable.

A direct uniform SLLN verifies the repair: for each eta-net, sup_K|P_mg_K-Pg_K|<=max_L|P_mg_L-Pg_L|+C eta(P_m||X||_2+M_P). On the intersection of probability-one SLLN events for a countable sequence of finite nets and ||X||, limsup is <=2 C eta M_P for every net scale; letting eta decreases to 0 gives zero.
findings.dependency_and_impact: Theorem 8 invokes Theorem 11 explicitly for the first term of equation (12) and for the recovery sequence. The printed proof therefore has a core derivation gap. The local correction above validates the needed uniform convergence; on the feasible compact class the minimizer-subsequence conclusion survives.
findings.counterevidence: This does not refute the assertion of Theorem 11 or the properly qualified consistency result. Their corrected proofs are supplied above. No inference of a new mathematical flaw from missing code is involved.
findings.assessment_note: supported major finding with scoped counterexample and counterevidence

findings.title: Theorem 14's deterministic Rademacher bound uses an empirical L1 radius where an L2 radius is required
findings.location: Theorem 14, p24; displayed complexity estimate and definition of c_P,m, p25
findings.claim: The proof bounds empirical Rademacher complexity by inf_epsilon {epsilon+c_P,m sqrt((2/m) log N(F,||.||_{1,X_m},epsilon))}, with c_P,m=sup_K (1/m) sum_i g_K(x_i).

counterexample.class_admissibility: Each g_j is the gauge of a positive-definite ellipsoid K_j. Since g_j(x)<=||x||_2, K_j contains B^16; take r_C=1. The class is finite. D(K,L)=sup_{||u||=1}|g_K(u)-g_L(u)| is a metric on it and yields the required Lipschitz property with C_C=1. The sample lies in the unit ball.
counterexample.empirical_radius: On the sample, g_j(e_i)=1 for i=j and tau otherwise. Thus c_P,m=(1+15 tau)/16=203/3200.
counterexample.rademacher_exact: For Rademacher signs sigma_i, max_j sum_i sigma_i g_j(e_i)=tau sum_i sigma_i+(1-tau)max_j sigma_j. Taking expectations gives R=(999/16000)(1-2^(1-16))=(999/16000)(32767/32768).
counterexample.covering_exact: Distinct evaluation vectors have empirical L1 distance 2(1-tau)/16. With centres in this finite function class the covering number is 16 at all sufficiently small positive radii. Taking epsilon decreases to 0 in the asserted bound yields at most (203/3200)sqrt(log(16)/8).
counterexample.strict_analytic_contradiction: log16<3 and sqrt(3/8)<5/8, so the proposed limiting upper bound is <1015/25600<1/25. In contrast R>(999/16000)(31/32)=30969/512000>3/50. Thus the deterministic inequality is false.
counterexample.iid_scope: If desired the specified ordered sample has positive probability under the uniform distribution on {e_1,...,e_16}; no atypical sample is excluded by a deterministic complexity estimate.

corrected_proof: For a finite net with N evaluation vectors v_j, the finite-class exponential-moment bound is E max_j (1/m)sum_i sigma_i v_{j,i}<=a_2 sqrt(2 logN/m), where a_2=max_j[(1/m)sum_i v_{j,i}^2]^(1/2).
An empirical L1 epsilon approximation contributes at most epsilon to the signed empirical average, so the covering metric may remain L1; the amplitude factor must be an L2 radius.
A valid class-wide replacement is a_2(X_m)=sup_K[(1/m)sum_i g_K(x_i)^2]^(1/2). Under 0<=g_K(x_i)<=1/r_C, a_2<=sqrt(c_P,m/r_C)<=1/r_C.

Consequently using 1/r_C supplies a safe nonadaptive radius. The parameterized families in Corollaries 6-8 have separately checkable finite-dimensional entropy bounds, but their stated use of the same c_P,m inherits this derivation issue.
findings.dependency_and_impact: This invalidates the proof's specific data-dependent complexity estimate underlying the learning guarantees. It is separate from the bracketing defect and from the convex-body entropy defect.
findings.counterevidence: The finite example directly refutes the displayed deterministic bound, not the complete high-probability inequality including its additive concentration term. The theorem statement describes c_P,m only generically before the proof defines it. No claim is made that every safe-constant formulation of Theorem 14 is false.
findings.assessment_note: supported major finding with scoped counterexample and counterevidence

findings.title: Corollary 5 is derived from a false logarithmic entropy estimate for unrestricted convex bodies
findings.location: Corollary 5 proof, last part of p26 and entropy conclusion on p27
findings.claim: The proof states log N(C(r),d_H,epsilon)<=c(d-1)/2 log(R_r/epsilon) for all bounded convex bodies C(r)={K subset R_r B^d}, then uses log|C_epsilon^d| <= up to constants d log(R_r/epsilon) to obtain its sample rate.

counterexample.fixed_parameters: Fix d=2 and r=1/4, so the paper's R_r=(d+1)/(r^(d-1) kappa_(d-1)) equals 6. Let n>=7 and let u_1,...,u_n be equally spaced directions on the unit circle.
counterexample.packing_family: For each subset A subset {1,...,n}, define K_A=conv((1/2)B^2  union  {u_j:j in A}). Every K_A is a compact convex star body with nonempty interior, contains (1/2)B^2 and lies inside B^2 subset 6B^2. Thus all 2^n bodies lie in the quoted class C(r).
counterexample.separation: If A and B differ at index j, say j in A\B, then h_{K_A}(u_j)=1, whereas h_{K_B}(u_j)<=max{1/2,cos(2pi/n)}=cos(2pi/n). Hence d_H(K_A,K_B)>=h_n:=1-cos(2pi/n)>0.
counterexample.covering_lower_bound: An h_n/3-ball can contain at most one of these bodies, by the triangle inequality. Therefore log N(C(r),d_H,h_n/3)>=n log2.
counterexample.contradiction: Since h_n=2sin^2(pi/n), 8/n^2<=h_n<=2pi^2/n^2. At epsilon=h_n/3, the asserted logarithmic upper bound grows only O(log n), whereas the explicit packing requires n log2. No constant depending only on d can make the printed estimate valid for all small epsilon.
counterexample.volume_scope: This example refutes the larger-class entropy estimate that is explicitly used in the proof; it is not presented as a direct counterexample to the final probability bound on the volume-normalized union class.

associated_local_proof_errors: The radial function of a union is max_i rho_{K_i}, not the minimum printed on p26. The gauge of a union is min_i g_{K_i}. The reciprocal-to-maximum equality printed on p27 is also not an equality.

For matched components, the correct direct radial estimate is delta(union K_i,union L_i)<=max_i delta(K_i,L_i). For convex components with rB subset K_i,L_i subset RB, inclusions K_i subset L_i+hB subset (1+h/r)L_i and the reverse give delta(K_i,L_i)<=(R/r)d_H(K_i,L_i). This avoids the printed reciprocal manipulation.

Intersecting an arbitrary ambient epsilon-cover with a subclass need not leave a cover. Choosing representatives from the subclass for each intersecting ambient ball gives a valid cover at twice the radius, as the paper's Proposition 6 permits.
The number of component choices is safely bounded by N^L. The asserted exact binomial cardinality overlooks repetitions/equal unions and is not needed for a safe upper bound.
findings.dependency_and_impact: The claimed entropy order is the decisive issue: repairing union identities and cover centres alone does not establish the stated Corollary 5 rate for an unrestricted convex-body family. A correct nonparametric entropy analysis or a restricted finite-dimensional family is needed.
findings.counterevidence: This does not invalidate the earlier existence or consistency conclusions, which use only finite covers rather than this quantitative entropy order. It also does not refute the independent finite-dimensional parameter counts for ellipsoids, bounded-vertex polytopes or linear images of Schatten balls.
findings.assessment_note: supported major finding with scoped counterexample and counterevidence

findings.title: Proposition 7 lacks a normalization or upper bound on the likelihood
findings.location: Proposition 7 and the following posterior-TV consequence, p31
findings.claim: With only real Phi and finite normalizers, the proposition asserts TV(mu_P1,mu_P2)^2<=2 KL(P1||P2)/Z_P1^2.

counterexample.data: On R take P1=delta_0 and P2=(delta_0+delta_1)/2. Then P1 is absolutely continuous with respect to P2 and KL(P1||P2)=log2. Let Phi(x;y) identically -log4.
counterexample.checks: The likelihood is constantly 4, so Z_P1=Z_P2=4 and both posteriors equal their corresponding priors. The left side is (1/2)^2=1/4; the right side is (log2)/8<1/4.
counterexample.principle: Multiplying a likelihood by a positive constant leaves both posteriors unchanged, but changes the claimed upper bound by the inverse square of that constant.

corrected_proof: If 0<exp(-Phi)<=M<infinity, write t=TV(P1,P2). The L1 difference of the normalized likelihood-weighted densities gives TV(mu1,mu2)<=2Mt/Z_P1: use integral L|dP1-dP2|<=2Mt and |Z_P1-Z_P2|<=integral L|dP1-dP2|.
Pinsker then yields TV(mu1,mu2)^2<=2M^2 KL(P1||P2)/Z_P1^2. The printed constant is recovered when M=1, for example by adding Phi>=0.
The same bounded-likelihood qualification must be carried into the following moment-projection posterior bound.
findings.dependency_and_impact: A local missing-hypothesis correction. The statement as written is false, but the preceding Gaussian example uses a nonnegative potential and is not invalidated. This receipt does not assert a failure of the paper's central optimal-regularizer formula.
findings.assessment_note: supported minor finding with scoped counterexample and counterevidence

checked_results.claim: Theorems 8 and 9: consistency of empirical minimizers
reasoning: Theorems assert convergence of every convergent subsequence to a population minimizer and existence of such a subsequence. They do not assert that the entire sequence converges in the absence of uniqueness.
On a feasible compact class, the repaired uniform SLLN and continuity imply that if K_mj -> K, then F(K;P)<=F(L;P) for every L by empirical optimality, passage to the limit and uniform convergence.

Equicoercivity is automatic on the compact domain. Gamma convergence follows from uniform convergence and continuity; the constant sequence K_m=K is already a valid recovery sequence, though the paper constructs net approximations.

checked_results.claim: Theorem 12, Proposition 5 and Theorem 13: robustness to noise
reasoning: For the common-kernel class, each gauge is 1/r-Lipschitz in x. Under finite first moments, any coupling gives |E_Pg_K-E_Qg_K|<=E||X-Y||/r. Taking the infimum over couplings gives the stated W1 risk bound uniformly in K.
For independent X~P and Z~Q, coupling X to X+sigma Z gives W1(P,P*Q_sigma)<=sigma E||Z||, and therefore the noise-risk deviation tends to zero uniformly as sigma -> 0.
Theorem 13 explicitly supplies finite first moments of both laws. Also |E||X+sigma Z||-E||X|||<=sigma E||Z||, which validates the varying moment in its continuity argument.

The printed Theorem 12/Proposition 5 omit an explicit finite-first-moment clause when read in isolation; their displayed risk differences should be read in the finite-risk setting. No separate major finding is based on this because the actual minimizer theorem states the needed moments.
The p23 prose mentions finite second moment, but the actual theorem and argument need only the stated first moments. This stronger prose description is not a counterexample.
Uniqueness is not assumed, so only minimizer-subsequence convergence is claimed; the noise need not be Gaussian.

For ellipsoids A(B), rI<=A<=RI gives the required inner/outer balls, and d_H(A(B),D(B))<=||A-D||. A volumetric packing argument in the d(d+1)/2 dimensional space of symmetric matrices supplies the logarithmic metric entropy order; merely naming a manifold is not needed.

For polytopes with at most T vertices inside RB, discretizing each vertex gives log-cover order at most Td log(constant R/epsilon); convex-hull formation does not increase the maximum matching vertex distance. Restricting to those containing rB uses the factor-two cover-centre adjustment.

For Schatten-ball images, h_{L(B_Sp)}(u)=||L^T u||_{S_p_tilde}; the lower support bound yields rB inclusion and the operator norm gives RB inclusion. Duality verifies d_H(L(B),A(B))<=||L-A||_{S_p,2}. The ambient normed space has dimension dq^2, so a volume packing gives the claimed entropy order.
These geometric checks do not remove L2's problem with the common empirical-radius factor in the learning bounds. No author code or experiments are needed for these finite-dimensional checks.

checked_results.claim: Dictionary formulas on p29: bounded local corrections already encountered
reasoning: The explanatory first display writes z=Ax, whereas the following derivation correctly uses x=Az; the latter is the dimensionally appropriate gauge constraint.
For the usual symmetric l1 ball, A(B_l1)=conv{+/-A_1,...,+/-A_p}, not conv{A_1,...,A_p}. A=[1] gives [-1,1] versus the printed singleton {1}; full rank and unit-column conditions hold.

Consequently the safe vertex count is at most 2p, not p. This preserves the order of the stated bound up to absolute constants, once the common L2-radius issue is repaired. These are local formula corrections, not additional core failure claims.

The paper identifies posterior log-concavity only under appropriate likelihood conditions; convexity of the negative log likelihood together with the convex regularizer is sufficient. No arbitrary nonlinear forward-map log-concavity claim is attributed to it.

Section 8 describes numerical algorithms for learning general star-body regularizers and downstream task performance as future work. This theoretical treatment is not assessed as though it promised an implemented empirical benchmark.
